items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: I had plenty of wind in those days, but still, down there, the wind was hard, you know? And Toscanini didn’t budge, didn’t budge. He just kept conducting.

ctx.x: Stokowski. Well let me tell you about the two conductors. They used to alternate. One week on the broadcast Toscanini conducted. The next week Stokowski. And they alternated. Now we premiered the Shostakovitch Seventh Symphony. It can be bought. It was taken off the air. And I had to borrow a special bass clarinet that went down to the low C. Today they all go to the low C. So I was tipped off by the bassoon player, that Mike Guerra in Philadelphia, had one, it went to the low C. I called him and he says, “Yes…
